review_notes: Read the whole target file and the analogous theorem `mollifySlice_ae_prod_sub_eq_intervalIntegral` and its helper lemmas in JointMeasurable.lean (lines ~388–589), which the target imports. The target's product-form theorem repeats that theorem's first ~75 proof lines almost token for token. The only differences are that `mollifiedRHS` is inlined as `RHSfun` there and that the final swap targets a different order. The two helper lemmas are verbatim copies of private lemmas in the same imported file. Other repetition in the file (hz1/hz2, hproj1/hproj2, the filter_upwards extraction at the end) is short and I did not report it. I could not run Lean, so the refactor is untested. Two points are uncertain. `mollifiedRHS` would have to move into JointMeasurable (or an earlier file) so the shared lemma can use it. The unfolding of `mollifiedRHS` against the inline integrand is by `rfl`, but I did not compile it.

findings.problem: The proof repeats the long measure-theoretic argument of `CIV.mollifySlice_ae_prod_sub_eq_intervalIntegral` (JointMeasurable.lean, ~499–575) almost verbatim. Both proofs (1) get joint a.e.-strong measurability of `q` and of `mollifySlice` via `prod_restrict`/`volume_eq_prod`, (2) pull `f` back along the two `QuasiMeasurePreserving` projections, (3) get measurability of `g` from `aestronglyMeasurable_comparisonRHS` and `aestronglyMeasurable_intervalIntegral`, (4) show the `volume.restrict I` and plain interval integrals differ only on a null set, by the `hsubset`/`hnull`/`hIcI`/`hz1`/`hz2` argument, (5) check the per-`x` hypothesis from `mollifySlice_ae_ae_sub_eq_intervalIntegral`, and (6) apply `ae_prod_prod_eq_of_forall_ae_ae`. The old theorem then does an extra swap and Fubini extraction, and the target does a different one. The target's `hswap` block repeats the old one as well. Any change to the measurability or null-set bookkeeping has to be made twice, and the two copies already differ cosmetically (`RHSfun` against `mollifiedRHS`, `rw [hfdef, hgdef]`).
findings.proposed_change:
Move `mollifiedRHS` and the target's statement `mollifySlice_sub_eq_intervalIntegral_ae_prod` (the `∀ᵐ p ∂(volume.prod (μI.prod μI))` form) into JointMeasurable.lean, placed right before `mollifySlice_ae_prod_sub_eq_intervalIntegral`. Its proof is exactly lines 73–137 of the target. Then shorten `mollifySlice_ae_prod_sub_eq_intervalIntegral` to this:
  have hcross := mollifySlice_sub_eq_intervalIntegral_ae_prod hI hIoc hB hq heq hε hτ₀
  -- then only the `ae_of_ae_map … Prod.swap` step and the two `ae_ae_of_ae_prod` extractions remain, with the integrand unfolded definitionally (`mollifiedRHS` is the inlined sum).
In AnchorFubini.lean, import the lemma instead of reproving it, and delete lines 63–137. `ae_isReferenceTime_mollifySlice` already calls it by name, and the file already imports JointMeasurable, so no new imports are needed. Optionally factor the shared `hswap` step (a.e. on `Vec m × I × I` gives a.e. on `(I × I) × Vec m` via `Measure.prod_swap` and `ae_of_ae_map`) into a one-line lemma used by both theorems.
findings.benefit: The roughly 65-line measurability and null-set argument is stated and maintained once. The old theorem's proof shrinks to the swap and extraction. AnchorFubini.lean shrinks to its real content, the two Fubini orders for the anchor time. The two statements are also explicitly linked, where before they were only linked by being copies.

The only change is the name. The copies exist only because the originals are private. Two identical, independently maintained proofs (the `uIcc ⊆ I`, `Ioc ⊆ I` and `change … rw [h1, h2]` steps) are therefore in the library.
findings.proposed_change: In JointMeasurable.lean, remove `private` from `setIntegral_restrict_eq` and `intervalIntegral_restrict_eq` (or rename them to the `_of_subset`/`_of_mem` names). Delete lines 46–61 here. Any use then refers to the one shared lemma, and the `hsubset` step uses `intervalIntegral_restrict_eq`. If finding 1 is applied, the only user in this file disappears and the copies can simply be deleted.
findings.benefit: This removes about 16 duplicated lines. It also avoids two public lemmas with the same statement, which readers could not tell apart and which could drift apart.
